Yes. On 16 June the plant exceeded its 1250 kW contract limit twice, during the Monday-morning simultaneous start:

- Peak: **1324.4 kW** at 08:15, which is 1.06× the contract [data: get_demand]
- Two intervals over contract: 08:00 (1307.1 kW) and 08:15 (1324.4 kW) [data: get_demand]

Demand rose from ~310 kW at 06:30 to the peak within an hour as the SMT lines and ovens started together, then fell back below contract by 08:30. The rest of the day stayed under the limit (midday peak ~1082 kW). This is the S2 scenario.

According to the plant documents:

**Why off, not standby:** A reflow oven in standby draws 36% of its 70 kW rating — 25.2 kW — continuously for as long as it stays on, while producing nothing. A properly switched-off oven uses only about 340–350 kWh per oven-weekend. Standby is only justified when boards are inside the oven. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]

**Cost in incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20):** RF-02 was left in standby all weekend. Weekend energy was about 1,556 kWh versus about 346 kWh normal — an excess of about 1,210 kWh from that single oven. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]

Note: the off-schedule rule only flags this after 120 minutes above 20% of rating, so the saving comes from preventing it, not detecting it. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]

The documents give the excess in energy (≈1,210 kWh) but not a dollar cost figure.

answer:
According to SOP-03 (the load-shed playbook in EM-02), the shed order is:

1. **First shed:** EV charging (EV-01), paused 100% [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order]

2. **Never shed:** the server room (DC-01), running molders mid-cycle (IM-01 to IM-04), and reflow ovens with boards inside (RF-01 to RF-03) [unverified citation removed]

The remaining shed actions, in order after EV charging, are: delay the next burn-in loading (BI-01, BI-02), raise the chilled-water setpoint +1°C (CH-01, CH-02), and lower compressed-air pressure 0.5 bar (AC-01 to AC-03) [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order].
